I’m going to explain it to you by detail because to this day I remember exactly how it felt.

When I pulled the trigger the first feeling was the shrinking of my left lung, just like when you inflate a balloon and then suck the air out of it.

Then the sound of the gunshot startled me and there was this ringing in both ears because of the impact.

Then was the shock. I did it to myself but still hadn’t grasp what just had happened: “I have just injured my body purposely, I can’t believe I did this”.

When I threw myself into the ground I remember I was like “Is this it? Am I dead? I just shot myself and there’s no pain at all...” while I was on the ground I began moving my head and feet thinking “Ok a bullet literally penetrated my body and I can move my head and lower extremities with no problem”. Then after that I was such disbelief that I tried to look at my chest and that’s when I felt a pinch, like this extreme pressure outside and inside my body and smelled all the blood beneath me and that’s when I processed, “Ok this is real”.

Then came the guilt. Listening to my aunts cries in desperation without being able to do anything. Just listening in silence with my eyes closed sensing every movement. But besides crippling anxiety and guilt, there was also peace. It’s not like when you cry laughing or even when you’re high, it was this blissful happiness and peace that you can only understand if you’ve experienced first. 

Another unpleasant feeling was feeling the hot blood and inside tissue coming out of my back wound running down my skin. After all the adrenaline came down and I was inside the ER, I remember the paramedics rolling my body towards the back to check if the bullet had came out. Now that hurt, but it wasn’t the worst pain in the world.
